 Follow Us On: News Trending News Harsh Goenka questions how Indian tourists behave abroad after viral Vietnam video Harsh Goenka questions how Indian tourists behave abroad after viral Vietnam video
 A viral video of Indian tourists sitting on the floor and eating at a Vietnam airport has sparked a debate over civic sense and public etiquette. Harsh Goenka also shared the post.
 Advertisement A group of tourists were seen having food in an airport in Vietnam. (Photos: hvgoenka/X) By: India Today Trending Desk New Delhi , Nov 9, 2026 07:56 IST Last Updated Nov 9, 2026 07:56 IST Published by Srimoyee Chowdhury Nov 8, 2026 17:33 IST Airport floors are usually meant for walking, waiting and catching connecting flights. A group of Indian tourists, however, appeared to have found another use for one at an airport in Vietnam; sitting down for a meal.
 The video has drawn criticism online, with industrialist Harsh Goenka questioning the travellers' civic sense.
 The video, which has been circulating on social media, shows a group of Indian travellers sitting on the airport floor with food spread around them.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The sight has left several viewers unimpressed, with many questioning why public spaces are treated so casually, particularly in a foreign country.
 Reacting to the footage, Goenka shared it on X and pointed out that Vietnam has increasingly become a popular travel destination among Indian tourists. However, he expressed concern that such incidents could affect how Indian travellers are perceived internationally.
 The industrialist criticised the tourists for treating an international airport like a picnic spot, raising questions about basic cleanliness and civic etiquette.
 He also called out the practice of spreading food and littering in public spaces, questioning when Indians would learn to behave responsibly while travelling overseas.
 Watch the video here: Vietnam has become a favourite new destination for Indian travellers. But if we turn their airports into picnic spots, spreading food and litter, we risk becoming very unpopular tourists. When will we learn to travel with civic sense? https://t.co/pCSC63GHRH— Harsh Goenka (@hvgoenka) November 7, 2026 His post soon attracted considerable attention, with social media users joining the discussion and sharing their views on the incident. Several users criticised the group for disregarding public spaces and failing to maintain basic standards of cleanliness.
 One user went a step further, suggesting that authorities should identify such travellers and cancel their passports. The user argued that strict consequences, along with greater public awareness, were necessary to discourage such behaviour.
 Drawing a comparison with countries known for their strict public regulations, the user also pointed out that Indians would think twice before behaving similarly in places such as Singapore, where littering and violations of public rules can attract hefty penalties.
 The incident has once again brought the question of civic responsibility among Indian tourists into focus.
 While travelling abroad offers an opportunity to explore different cultures and destinations, social media users argued that respecting public spaces and following local rules should be part of the experience.
 For many, the debate was not simply about a group eating at an airport, but about the larger responsibility travellers carry when representing their country overseas. - Ends
